sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export competitiveness is structurally reinforced by low domestic production costs and government-mandated DMO pricing, insulating local miners from global cost inflation.
Nickel's long-term demand driver is the EV battery supply chain, with Indonesia's HPAL capacity expansion positioning it as the dominant low-cost producer despite price volatility.
The IDX energy complex benefits from a weakening IDR, which boosts rupiah-denominated earnings for exporters while US-listed peers face margin compression from stronger dollar input costs.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to Indonesian coal and nickel names on the back of sustained thermal coal demand from China/India and nickel price stabilization from Indonesia's ore quota discipline; ENRG and BYAN lead momentum, but rotate into ADMR and INCO for lower beta upside. Trim US-linked names as the ID/US divergence widens.

EV adoption in Indonesia is accelerating via downstream nickel processing and domestic bus mandates, making VKTR a direct beneficiary of local content rules and fleet electrification targets.

sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesia renewables names on local strength: VKTR (EV buses) and TOBA (geothermal) lead with domestic policy tailwinds, while US-listed peers lag. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural demand recovery is accelerating, driven by government cash transfers and improved agricultural incomes, lifting volume growth for FMCG staples with wide distribution networks.
Premiumization and health-conscious product launches are creating durable margin expansion opportunities for mid-cap players, as urban consumers trade up to functional and organic offerings.

Digital-first direct-to-consumer channels and e-commerce partnerships are reshaping distribution economics, enabling smaller brands to capture share from incumbents at lower customer acquisition costs
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names with strong rural distribution and digital channel exposure, as the sector's flat aggregate masks sharp idiosyncratic gains (AGAR +24.9%, UDNG +8.3%) driven by earnings beats and product innovation. Favor companies with pricing power in staples and premiumization in discretionary, while avoiding laggards with weak cash conversion. Position for Q3 volume recovery and margin tailwinds from lower input costs.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's infrastructure capex cycle is accelerating on new capital-city (IKN) and toll-road tenders, favoring small-cap contractors like TEBE and YPAS with high order-book-to-market ratios.
Telecom tower and data-center buildout remains a durable multi-year driver, lifting EXCL and LINK as operators expand 5G and edge capacity despite macro volatility.
US rate-sensitive infrastructure underperformance is a short-term headwind, but ID's domestic-demand resilience and rupiah stability keep local infra equities structurally bid.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in TEBE and YPAS after their 25% limit-up runs; both are small-cap contractors with order-book momentum that can sustain re-rating. Rotate out of LINK (19% pop) into EXCL or BRNA for relative value, as US infra weakness (-0.31%) is transient. Maintain neutral aggregate exposure, but add selectively on any 2-3% dip in liquid names like PACK or ASLI, given normal signal and ID outperformance.

SRAJ (+15.38%) and PEHA (+13.64%) signal momentum in pharma distribution and hospital supplies; add on pullbacks, but avoid US-linked laggards. Position for Q3 earnings catalysts, prioritizing firms with pricing power and government procurement ties.

Port and shipping rates are normalizing after pandemic spikes, but infrastructure investment in new ports and cold-chain facilities is creating durable cost advantages for integrated players.

Trim SHIP on cyclical risk. Keep overall sector weight neutral-to-overweight, prioritizing names with volume growth and margin recovery.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's pending crypto tax harmonization and exchange licensing under Bappebti is a structural catalyst for compliant, utility-driven tokens over speculative ones.
Global RWA tokenization (ONDO, RAIN) is compounding as institutional treasuries and Indonesian corporates seek on-chain yield alternatives to fiat deposits.
Liquid staking and restaking narratives (ETHFI, MORPHO) are gaining durable traction as DeFi leverage demand rises, independent of Bitcoin's price direction.
sectors.ai: Rotate into high-beta liquid alts (BTW, MORPHO, ETHFI) for near-term momentum, but keep core longs in yield-bearing RWA plays (ONDO, RAIN) as the durable bid. Trim ZEC/WLD into strength; the aggregate signal is normal, not euphoric, so add on dips rather than chase. Indonesia's regulatory clarity on digital assets remains a tailwind for compliant exchanges, favoring tokens with real utility over memetic names.
